prompt: Write a one-star review of the Grand Canyon from a visitor who feels it was too big.
response:
★☆☆☆☆ **Way Too Much Canyon, Not Enough Point**

I honestly don’t understand the hype. Everyone says it’s a "must-see," but nobody warns you about the sheer, overwhelming scale of this place. It’s not just big; it’s aggressively, uncomfortably massive. We drove four hours to get there, walked up to Mather Point, and were immediately hit with this suffocating sense of insignificance that lasted the entire trip. There is simply *too much* of it. Your eyes can’t even process where it ends; it just goes on forever in every direction until your brain kind of gives up.

I wanted a nice scenic view, maybe something I could actually focus on and appreciate. Instead, I got an endless, exhausting abyss that made me feel dizzy and strangely anxious. There’s no framing, no intimacy, just an unrelenting expanse of red rock that makes you feel like a speck of dust. After twenty minutes, I was completely desensitized. It all starts to look the same, just an infinite repetition of cliffs and voids.

The crowds don’t help either. Everyone’s jostling for the same sliver of railing, trying to capture something so incomprehensibly huge that it looks flat and meaningless in photos anyway. I left feeling drained, disoriented, and honestly a little depressed. If you want a landscape that respects human scale and doesn’t make you question your own existence, go somewhere else. The Grand Canyon is just too much canyon for one person to handle.
